overview: This paper proposes HeteroRL, a heterogeneous reinforcement learning framework that decouples rollout sampling and parameter learning, and introduces GEPO, a policy optimization algorithm that stabilizes asynchronous training under high network latency by replacing token/sample-level importance weights with group-level expectation weights to exponentially reduce variance.

modules.name: HeteroRL Configuration Manager
modules.description: Manages global experimental settings including network latency distributions (Lognormal, Weibull, Exponential), maximum tolerable delay bounds, staleness thresholds, and hardware topology configurations (Learner/Sampler node counts).

modules.name: Math Reasoning Data Processor
modules.description: Handles the loading and preprocessing of mathematical reasoning datasets (MATH, AMC, AIME). Formats prompts based on 'think' and 'non-think' modes, and applies tokenization with specific context length limits and system prompt templates.

modules.name: Network Latency Simulation Engine
modules.description: Simulates network delays in decentralized environments by generating stochastic delay times for model synchronization and data transfer. It controls the staleness gap (tau) between the sampler's behavior policy and the learner's target policy to emulate real-world heterogeneous network conditions.

modules.name: Asynchronous Rollout Sampler
modules.description: Implements the sampler node logic that continuously generates trajectory groups (G responses per prompt) using the stale policy. It manages the asynchronous generation loop, periodically checking for model parameter updates after simulated delay intervals without idling.

modules.name: Group Expectation Importance Weight Calculator
modules.description: Computes the core GEPO weight mechanism. It calculates the within-group normalized probability for each response, derives the group expectation of the proposal probability (sum of q squared divided by sum of q), and computes the ratio of the target policy probability to this group expectation denominator.

modules.name: Group Relative Advantage Calculator
modules.description: Computes the advantage function for each trajectory using group-wise statistics. It uses the within-group average reward as the baseline to normalize rewards, ensuring the advantage reflects relative performance within the group of responses for the same prompt.

modules.name: GEPO Loss Function Implementation
modules.description: Implements the policy gradient loss using the Group Expectation Importance Weights (GEIW). It contrasts with GRPO (token-level weights) and GSPO (sequence-level weights) by applying the group-level coefficient to the advantage-weighted log probabilities, optionally incorporating KL regularization.

modules.name: Asynchronous Learner Node
modules.description: Implements the central learner logic that asynchronously consumes rollout data from samplers. It manages a sliding window data buffer to filter out-of-date trajectories, performs gradient updates, and broadcasts updated model parameters back to sampler nodes at specified intervals.

modules.name: ZeroMQ Communication Toolkit
modules.description: Provides the real-world network communication infrastructure for distributed RL. Implements TCP/IP-based bidirectional endpoints for sending inference trajectories from samplers to learners and broadcasting synchronized model parameters from the learner to samplers.

modules.name: Localized Reward Computation Optimizer
modules.description: Optimizes the reward aggregation process by eliminating global communication overhead. Ensures that group statistics (mean and variance of rewards) are computed locally on the sampler or within the same data parallel rank, preventing blocking caused by slow nodes during all-gather operations.

modules.name: Training Stability Monitor
modules.description: Tracks and logs critical stability metrics during training, including the variance of importance weights, KL divergence between learner and sampler policies, gradient norms, and estimation errors of the expected advantage function. Visualizes the correlation between latency, KL, and variance explosion.

modules.name: Mathematical Reasoning Evaluator
modules.description: Evaluates model performance on mathematical benchmarks (MATH500, AMC23, AIME24/25). Calculates Pass@1 scores over multiple sampled responses and tracks both 'Best' and 'Last' performance to measure training stability and reward collapse.

modules.name: Importance Weight Ablation Framework
modules.description: Provides a flexible framework to switch between token-level (GRPO), sequence-level (GSPO), and group-level (GEPO) importance weighting mechanisms. Facilitates controlled ablation studies to isolate the impact of the importance weight granularity on gradient variance and stability.

modules.name: Hyperparameter Sensitivity Runner
modules.description: Automates the execution and analysis of sensitivity studies across key hyperparameters. Sweeps through group sizes, KL regularization coefficients, latency distributions, sampling temperatures, and top-p/top-k values to determine their impact on peak performance and best-to-last degradation.
